installPolicy.notes: Multiple installations use unique instance IDs and isolated executable/package roots. User data is shared only through versioned, explicitly compatible namespaces. Never overwrite a different instance's engine, config or package files.

bootloaderAdapters.notes: The muOS application launcher starts the installed muxapp. A QWASAR pre-frontend selector can choose an installed Void Desk instance and available engine; it does not replace or modify the handheld bootloader.
A desktop application launcher starts the QWASAR pre-frontend selector inside the already booted host OS.

Optional integration for selecting complete bootable OS/root filesystem installations only. GRUB does not select Pygame versus LÖVE inside an already running OS. Any generated entry requires explicit opt-in, backup, preview and rollback; never rewrite GRUB automatically during an ordinary app package install.

sessionTargets.description: Launch the optional Debian/Ubuntu XFCE desktop image on H700 or a supported desktop session on PC.

Standalone Python console with a restricted working directory and explicit environment.
Connect to a paired PC workstation; remote display and remote input are separate, explicit capabilities.

integrations.deviceRole: handheld or PC client when a supported client build exists
integrations.notes: Optional software-KVM adapter. It shares keyboard/mouse control between machines and is not a remote-display or video-stream protocol. The runtime must probe binary/platform support on both ends; if unavailable, offer the QWASAR Link remote-input adapter instead. Clipboard support depends on the host/display stack.
QWASAR-owned integration layer. InputLeap may be an optional backend for keyboard/mouse only; remote display and file transfer use separate authenticated channels.
Optional PC-only virtualization backend, detected through VBoxManage and host capability checks. VirtualBox 7.2 documentation lists Linux x86_64 hosts; do not advertise this on H700/muOS.

integrations.deviceRole: handheld or PC client where a supported endpoint exists
integrations.notes: Alternative software-KVM backend to probe alongside Input Leap. Select only after both endpoints, session type, encryption and input permissions pass compatibility checks. It does not provide remote display.

packageAdapters.notes: APT is confined to the optional Debian/Ubuntu image. If the image is not mounted/available, offer the trusted image installer or report unavailable.
Separate PC-only adapter. It requires an explicit user/admin prompt, names the host package database and exact packages, serializes operations and never runs arbitrary module commands.
APT must never target the muOS Buildroot host. Use firmware packages and the muOS application lifecycle instead.

featureManagement.disableSemantics: Disable removes a contribution from the active UI/profile but does not uninstall its files. Providers and background jobs owned solely by the disabled module must stop cleanly; shared dependencies remain active while referenced. Hidden affects presentation only. Installed, enabled, visible, available and running are separate states.

tools.purpose: Read-only audit of UI schemas, manifests, module inventory, duplicate/orphan IDs, unresolved routes/actions/providers, missing assets, dependency graphs, engine/platform compatibility, permissions, package manifests and profile validity.
Profile-level control center to enable/disable modules, workspaces, sections, widgets, menu entries and global panels; preview, reorder, hide/show and restore defaults without uninstalling packages.
